note: Controls are ranked per the NIOSH hierarchy of controls (Elimination > Substitution > Engineering controls > Administrative controls > PPE). Verified: research/sources.md, access date 2026-10-27.

hierarchyLabels.substitution: Substitution — replace with something less hazardous
hierarchyLabels.engineering: Engineering controls — isolate people from the hazard
hierarchyLabels.administrative: Administrative controls — change how people work
hierarchyLabels.ppe: PPE — protect the individual worker (last line)

tasks.prompt: Rank these controls for overhanging pallets from most to least effective, using the hierarchy of controls.

controls.text: Hi-vis vests for everyone in the aisle
Rack layout change: deeper beams and load stops so pallets cannot sit past the edge
Monthly 'watch your load overhang' toolbox talk
Put-away process check: a pallet that cannot sit square is returned to the floor, never racked (removes the overhang state)
Weekly supervisor spot-checks of beam edges

tasks.why: Eliminating the overhang state beats detecting it; load stops (engineering) beat any amount of checking; spot-checks and talks are administrative; vests protect against consequences, not causes.

tasks.prompt: Rank these controls for the frayed charging cable.

controls.text: Face shield and gloves for anyone near the charger
Replace the cable and fit a strain-relief gland so the bend cannot fray it again (removes the damage mechanism)
Interlock: charger will not energize with a faulted cable (engineering)
Weekly visual check of charging equipment by a named owner

tasks.why: Removing the damage mechanism and adding an interlock are the durable fixes; checks and signs manage risk; PPE is the last line for residual risk.

tasks.hazard: Misaligned convex mirror at the blind corner
tasks.prompt: Rank these controls for the misaligned mirror.

controls.text: Sticker on the mirror: 'Check alignment weekly'
Re-align the mirror and add it to a weekly pre-shift equipment walk with a named owner (keeps it true)
Remove the blind corner: re-route the aisle end or fit a wide-angle camera with an in-cab display (removes the reliance on the mirror)
Reminder to drivers to 'double-check the mirror'

tasks.why: Removing the blind corner eliminates the reliance on any single device; a named-owner walk keeps the mirror honest; horns, stickers and reminders are the weakest tiers here.

isItTraining.because: A check with a named owner is a system fix; drivers were behaving correctly given a lying mirror.
The put-away decision under time pressure can be coached — but load stops (engineering) remove the failure mode entirely. Do both.
Practice and feedback help — yet ask why the lane route feels slower, and fix the layout or the expectation-setting that rewards the shortcut.
